While building a start element from attacker-controlled XML, libxml2 allocates an `xmlNs` object for one namespace declaration. ASan's allocation stack points to this exact call through start-element handling.

After parsing entity content, libxml2 stores the resulting node list on the entity definition. In reader mode this retains nodes whose namespace binding still aliases namespace state inherited from the surrounding reader-owned tree instead of detaching it first.

When the reader advances and `reader->entNr == 0`, it unlinks the previous node and frees it because the node is not preserved. The ASan free stack records this exact cleanup call site before the namespace list is released.

Freeing the old reader node releases the namespace list attached to that original element. ASan identifies this namespace-free path as the freeing context for the address later read in `xmlStaticCopyNode`.
A later entity reference expansion in reader mode reloads the retained child list from the entity object, reintroducing a node whose `ns` pointer still aliases the namespace freed in step 4.

`xmlDocCopyNode(cur, ctxt->myDoc, 1)` reaches namespace fixup for the copied element, looks up the original namespace with `xmlSearchNs`, and then dereferences `ns->href` and `ns->prefix`. That `ns` points into the xmlNs object freed by `xmlTextReaderFreeNode`, producing the observed heap-use-after-free read.
